text.p: Brisbane broker Morgan Stockbroking said it was rating shares of metal recycler Simsmetal Ltd a buy based on a strong outlook for base metals and the company's leverage to metal prices.
"We maintain our buy recommendation given our positive outlook for base metals and Simsmetal's high leverage to metal prices," Morgan's metal analysts said in a research report.
Asian ferrous scrap prices have recovered from their lows of last November with the destocking cycle of Asian electric-arc furnace producers seemingly complete, the Morgan report said.

"Trend prices are expected to increase moderately out to the year 2000 as increasing amounts of obsolete scrap are utilised to meet rising demand," the report said. A stronger Australian economy and an upturn in the housing sector should drive stronger results from Sims Aluminium, Conex and Australian scrap operations in the current year ended June 30, 1997, it said.
"Recent trading in Australia has been flat but the United Kingdom and United States operations have seen slight improvement in volumes," the Morgan analysts said.
Morgan forecasting a net profit for the current year of A$33.6 million rising to A$48.6 million in 1997/98.
The current year forecast compared with Simsmetal's reported net profit of A$46.7 million in the year to June 30, 1996.
Simsmetal's share price at the time the report was written was A$8.12. The stock was quoted at A$8.52 at midday on Tuesday, up eight cents from Monday's close.
